text:
maya: FYI Acme is seeing a spike in 502/504s for hosted inference since ~09:40 PST. They report streaming requests timing out and SDK retry loops. Example error: "stream closed with status 504". Customer page: https://acme.example/app (asked to DM).

maya: Attaching their SDK logs (snip) and our gateway dashboard shows p95 latency jump from 120ms -> 1.8s at 09:41. No large CPU/GPU pressure on dedicated pools.

dan: Do we have request_ids for the failed requests? Also check if there were any deploys or infra config changes around 09:35-09:45.

maya: Got a few request ids from the SDK: req_01H8F2X9, req_01H8F31A, req_01H8F3ZQ. Pasting brief log lines from client: 
```
[2026-03-17T09:41:02Z] WARN retrying request req_01H8F2X9 after 504
[2026-03-17T09:41:03Z] INFO auth: token refresh triggered, new token obtained
[2026-03-17T09:41:03Z] WARN connection reset during streaming
```

maya: Customer also reported they had a simultaneous job that rotated API keys (internal) around same time. They suspect auth churn.

ben: ops-bot, any infra deploys?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: roll/edge-proxy-v2 at 2026-03-17T09:40:22Z (user: infra-deploy). Change: lowered idle keepalive to 10s and aggressive connection eviction to reduce sticky conns.

carmen: That keepalive/eviction change + customer-side token refresh fanout could cause a thundering herd of new TLS handshakes and simultaneous auth handoffs, leading to short-term gateway overload and 5xx. We saw similar patterns last year.

dan: Agreed. The stacktrace in gateway logs for req_01H8F2X9 shows upstream backend returned "deadline exceeded" and connection pool hit max waiters. Sending snippet: 
```
[gateway] request=req_01H8F2X9 backend=runtime-01 error="upstream deadline exceeded" pool_waiters=48
```

dan: Looks like connection pool starvation with lots of reconnects.

maya: Customer is asking for repro steps they can do to confirm it's on our side. What should I recommend?

ben: Short repro they can run from their env: 
1) Start 50 concurrent streaming calls with the current SDK (default keepalives).
2) Trigger a programmatic token rotation in their app (single call to rotate keys).
3) Observe increase in 5xx/504 and connection resets.

ben: Example curl (non-streaming) to reproduce a simple token refresh handshake storm: 
```
for i in {1..50}; do \
  TOKEN=$(rotate_token_cmd) && \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

carmen: For mitigation tell customer: reduce concurrency during rotation, add jitter to token refresh, and upgrade to SDK v1.4.2 which adds connect reuse and random jitter on refresh. Also we've temporarily rolled back the edge-proxy keepalive change to mitigate immediate impact.

ops-bot: infra-note: rolled back roll/edge-proxy-v2 at 2026-03-17T09:52:10Z per infra-deploy. Monitoring for p95 returning to baseline.

maya: I've told Acme to pause key rotation and switch to SDK v1.4.2 with the env var REDWOOD_REFRESH_JITTER=1.5s. They're applying and will run repro.

dan: I'm going to increase connection pool size on gateway for a short window and add a hotfix to ensure auth refreshes don't close idle connections immediately. Assigning to eng-runtime for a patch.

ben: Filed internal ticket INF-4729 with logs and suggested patch. Will link to customer ticket CS-11987.

maya: Customer updated: after switching to SDK v1.4.2 and pausing rotation, errors dropped to near zero. They still saw a couple of 502s during the rollback window. Customer thanks the team and asked for a writeup on recommended best practices for token rotation.

carmen: I'll draft a short KB: include: stagger rotations, add jitter, throttle concurrency during rotation, and prefer long-lived connection reuse.

dan: Next steps: eng-runtime to push a small fix (protective backoff on pool eviction) and infra to validate keepalive settings. Keep customer posted in CS-11987.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer thread and close this Slack thread after the KB is published. :white_check_mark:
